transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~57m
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (SilverHarbor - Head of Platform), Liam Ortega (SilverHarbor - SRE), Priya Desai (SilverHarbor - Procurement)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
- Renewal discussion focused on committed capacity uplift for EU region and pilot in APAC edge.
- Primary concerns: latency SLOs, private VPC onboarding time, and KMS/integration for key rotation.
- Agreed to run a short perf pilot and exchange security docs; Redwood to send commitment quote with burst lanes.

Topics: capacity uplift, region activation (EU -> APAC), SLA targets, procurement timeline, security/KMS, pilot runbook

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, uh we'll wait another 30 seconds for folks to pop in but, um, quick agenda — renewal numbers, region rollout timeline, and then Marcus will walk through the perf plan.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: sounds good, thanks Jamie. we're mostly here wrt timeline, we have fiscal cutoffs and procurement slots, so wanna make sure the dates line up.
[00:26] Jamie Chen: totally. so just to be explicit: you're looking at bumping committed capacity by roughly 2.5x in EU and adding an APAC small cluster for latency sensitive endpoints, correct?
[00:36] Liam Ortega: yeah that's the ask, we want lower p95 for inference in Sydney and also a fallback plan if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[00:42] Marcus Patel: right, so the default pattern is we can provision a dedicated geocluster in ap-southeast with reserved capacity and an autoscale burst lane. one note — if you're latency bound we recommend smaller batch sizes for that route, and prefix/K V cache tuning.
[00:55] Liam Ortega: sorry did you say K V cash?
[00:57] Marcus Patel: (laughs) yeah k v cache, the prefix cache that keeps the KV state warm — my bad, transcription will say like K V cash sometimes.
[01:05] Priya Desai: quick question on procurement: do we need a separate PO for Hosted vs Dedicated, or is that wrapped in the committed contract?
[01:12] Jamie Chen: good question. we typically structure as one commitment contract for Dedicated capacity and then an attachment for burst usage; procurement side we can produce a single PO that references the contract, i'll include contract language in the quote.
[01:24] Aisha Khan: what's the SLA delta if we go Dedicated vs Hosted? our product team wants 99.9 p99 for customer-facing calls.
[01:34] Marcus Patel: Dedicated gives you a much tighter SLO — it's easier to guarantee p99 under dedicated pools since you're not contending with noisy tenants. hosted api has a documented SLA but the practical p99 for heavy tail workloads is generally looser. for 99.9 p99 we'd recommend Dedicated with sane failover to hosted as a fallback.
[01:50] Liam Ortega: and region failover? if eu cluster has outage, requests should go to us-west or hosted? what's the plan?
[01:57] Marcus Patel: smart routing policy — we'll set preferred route eu-dedicated, fallback to hosted in nearby region (us-west) or to a lighter quantized variant if you want cost control. the orchestration supports automatic fallback and we can configure canary rollouts to validate.
[02:12] Aisha Khan: is there additional egress billing when we failover cross-region? we have bank compliance concerns.
[02:20] Jamie Chen: yeah cross-region egress is a thing; i'll put a few scenarios in the quote showing net delta on monthly egress and the cost of cross-region fallback. also if you go VPC private, we have options to keep egress inside your network peer — that will change the architecture slightly.
[02:36] Priya Desai: we need SOC2 evidence plus encryption at rest with customer KMS. do you support customer-managed keys or HSM?
[02:44] Marcus Patel: we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS) — there might be an extra ops step for rotation but yes it's supported. we'll include certs and the SOC2 summary docs; expect Marcus to share the compliance pack.
[02:58] Jamie Chen: i'll attach SOC2, iso docs, and a short runbook for key rotation.
[03:03] Aisha Khan: timeline — ideally we want region live before Dec 15, because of our holiday campaign. is that realistic?
[03:10] Marcus Patel: depends on VPC onboarding. If you want Private VPC and dedicated, typical lead time is 3-4 weeks for EU region provisioning once we have network peering and KMS access; Hosted-only ramp can be faster (under a week). so Dec 15 is tight but doable if we start this week.
[03:25] Liam Ortega: ok so next steps: export traces and sample payloads for Marcus. we have a specific flow that keeps context > 2k tokens, hope that doesn't blow up cost.
[03:35] Marcus Patel: makes sense — sequence length distribution will inform whether we should recommend quantized variants or a higher-memory kernel; sometimes a slightly larger model is cheaper because of cache hit rates, weird but true.
[03:46] Aisha Khan: can you explain that again? larger model cheaper?
[03:49] Marcus Patel: yeah so if smaller model forces more tokens to be re-sent due to hallucination or bad few-shot prompts, net tokens can go up. also kernel efficiency and per-token throughput differ. we'll run cost-per-call sims with your traces.
[04:03] Jamie Chen: and we'll run a short pilot — Marcus will provision a small eu-dedicated cluster and an apac pilot, run your traces for 48 hours and hand back latency histograms + cost delta.
[04:14] Priya Desai: procurement will need options: 12-month commitment vs 6-month with higher run rate. what's historically chosen by other fintech customers?
[04:23] Jamie Chen: many mid-market finance customers do 12-month commitments with staged top-ups; some prefer 6-month to keep flexibility but pay more. i'll include both options in a CFR-style table with effective per-token rates.
[04:34] Aisha Khan: we also have a security review board who will insist on SSO and RBAC mappings; can you support SAML + SCIM?
[04:42] Marcus Patel: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; for RBAC we give role-based controls down to token-level in Console — though if you have custom roles we can map via SCIM. i'll include a doc with available roles.
[04:55] Liam Ortega: minute detail — how do you handle model rollouts? we can't tolerate a regression in hallucination rates.
[05:02] Marcus Patel: rollout features: canary, A/B comparisons, and automatic fallback to pinned model version. Redwood Optimize can run evaluation suites against your prompt set and fire regression alerts. we'll show an example in the pilot.
[05:15] Aisha Khan: who owns the regression threshold? we need to set an SLO for output quality not just latency.
[05:22] Jamie Chen: typically product+ml teams set quality thresholds; we can instrument quality metrics and tie alerts to rollbacks. we'll draft a proposal for an acceptance window for the pilot.
[05:32] [07:10] Speaker 1: (mumbling) sorry joining late — heard about KMS question — for HSM integration, is there a certificate exchange?
[05:40] Marcus Patel: yes we do a cert exchange and service account provisioning, i'll walk through the steps in the compliance pack.
[05:46] [10:05] Aisha Khan: procurement question — is the quote fixed or do you have escalation clauses for cloud cost increases?
[05:52] Jamie Chen: we include standard escalation language; for long-term commitments we can layer a fixed-rate arrangement for the committed tokens and adjust for pass-through egress or unique cloud surcharges. we'll show a model.
[06:03] Liam Ortega: on the technical checklist, can you confirm whether you provide KV cache metrics and a dashboard? we need to instrument the cache hit rate.
[06:12] Marcus Patel: yes we emit token-level metrics, cache hit/miss, per-route latency, and per-model tail latency. Console also exposes traces and token-level cost. we'll give you dashboard links in the pilot report.
[06:24] Aisha Khan: which teams will be involved on your side during the pilot?
[06:30] Jamie Chen: it'll be me for contract and program mgmt, Marcus for infra and the bench runs, and if needed we can pull an SRE for deeper network setup.
[06:38] Priya Desai: do you have any references for similar finance customers who've done eu+apac pilots?
[06:44] Jamie Chen: yes i'll include a sanitized case study; names are a bit constrained by NDA but i'll provide high level numbers and outcomes.
[06:50] Marcus Patel: one operational note — for apac we recommend colocated edge nodes for lower cold-start latencies. depends on your session stickiness.
[06:58] Liam Ortega: ok i think we can do the sample traces today. we'll also list the required approvers for procurement.
[07:05] Jamie Chen: perfect. to recap — Redwood will: send a quote with 12m and 6m options, share SOC2/compliance pack, Marcus will prepare perf runbook and request traces, and we'll schedule a 48-hour pilot targeted for week of Nov 17. customer will: send traces, confirm approvers, and provide KMS details if Private is chosen.
[07:27] Aisha Khan: sounds good. one last thing — do you support custom quantization profiles? some of our models are very latency-sensitive.
[07:35] Marcus Patel: yes we do per-model quantization recommendations as part of Redwood Optimize; for private setups we can ship custom kernels or tuned kernels if needed.
[07:44] Priya Desai: procurement note: can you include billing contact and invoicing cadence in the quote?
[07:49] Jamie Chen: yes will include annual vs quarterly invoicing options and contact details.
[07:54] Jamie Chen: alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments. any blockers?
[07:58] Aisha Khan: no blockers from our side; thanks all.
[08:02] Jamie Chen: great, talk soon. bye.
